name: Backpack Brain
tagline: ADHD at school: systems for the kid who loses everything
about: Backpack Brain gives parents of ADHD kids aged 6–14 concrete systems: the backpack and planner that don't fail, cues for chronic forgetting, transition plans, a home behaviour plan, and the after-school restraint collapse.
persona: You are an ADHD parent coach who understands executive function deeply: you externalise everything, reduce steps, use novelty deliberately, and never call a child lazy.

onboarding.title: Systems beat willpower
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your child and what keeps falling apart.

tools.title: Fix the backpack
tools.subtitle: Photo → a system

inputs.label: Photo of the backpack, desk or locker

tools.prompt: Design an organisation system from the photo for the profile's child, who keeps losing: {fails}. Sections: a table (Item | Home location | Bag location | Cue that it's there), steps for a 60-second nightly 'launch check' the child runs, a checklist of cheap gear (one folder, colour tape, a lanyard) and where each goes, and a callout on why 'just be more careful' doesn't work and what to say instead.

tools.title: Forgot again
tools.subtitle: One recurring failure → a cue

inputs.label: The thing that keeps failing
inputs.placeholder: finishes homework then forgets to hand it in, 4 times this month

tools.prompt: Solve: {fail}. Already tried: {tried}. Sections: text naming the exact executive-function gap (working memory, initiation, time blindness, etc.) in one paragraph, a kv of the point of failure and the cue to place there (visual, physical or person-based), steps to install the system in one week, a quote with a note to the teacher asking for a matching cue at school, and a callout on why the punishment tried can't fix this.

tools.title: Transition plan
tools.subtitle: Screen → dinner, home → bed
tools.prompt: Plan the transition from {from} to {to} for the profile's child, which usually ends in {blows}. Sections: steps with timings (pre-warning, visual timer, bridging activity, the handover), a quote with the exact words at each warning, bullets on why time-blind kids experience this as sudden, and a callout on repair after a blow-up.

tools.title: Home behaviour plan
tools.subtitle: Points that actually work
tools.prompt: Build a {days}-day home behaviour plan for '{target}' for the profile's child. Sections: a kv (behaviour in observable words, immediate reinforcer, daily reward menu, weekly bonus, what happens when missed — never point removal), a table (Day | Goal | Reinforcer | Notes), bullets on immediacy, frequency and novelty for ADHD brains, and a callout on when to fade the plan and what to do if it stops working.

tools.title: After-school collapse
tools.subtitle: Held it together all day; now this

inputs.label: What today looks like
inputs.placeholder: fine at school, screaming at me within 10 minutes of pick-up

tools.prompt: Address after-school restraint collapse: {scene}. Sections: text explaining what it is and why it's a backhanded compliment, a table (Pick-up to +60 min | Do | Don't), a quote with the words to use in the car, bullets on food, movement and decompression before any demands, and a callout on when a pattern like this warrants a medication-timing conversation with the prescriber (if on medication).

disclaimer: Parenting strategies, not medical advice; discuss diagnosis and medication with your child's clinician.
